content: Individuals with a known allergy to eggs or other components of the influenza vaccine should not receive the vaccine. A history of Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) occurring within six weeks of a previous influenza vaccination is considered a precaution for subsequent influenza vaccine administration. Annual influenza vaccination is recommended for all individuals aged six months and older who do not have medical contraindications. This includes all healthcare personnel (HCP) without contraindications. The influenza vaccine is updated annually, with one or more vaccine strains revised almost every year to match circulating viruses. Additionally, antibody levels decline over the year following vaccination, which is why annual vaccination with the current season's formulation is recommended. It is safe and appropriate to begin annual vaccination as soon as the vaccine becomes available each season. In situations of limited vaccine supply, HCP should be prioritized for vaccination. Two types of influenza vaccines are available. The live attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) is administered intranasally and is approved for use in healthy, non-pregnant individuals aged 2–49 years. The trivalent inactivated vaccine (TIV) is administered via intramuscular injection and can be given to anyone aged six months and older. Both vaccine types contain virus strains selected to elicit a protective immune response against the wild-type viruses most likely to circulate during the upcoming influenza season. The use of LAIV among HCP who care for patients in protective inpatient environments has been a theoretical concern. However, there have been no reported cases of LAIV transmission in healthcare settings. LAIV can be used by HCP in any setting except for those who care for severely immunocompromised hospitalized patients requiring protective environments. HCP who are themselves at high risk for influenza complications, are pregnant, or are aged 50 years or older should not receive LAIV and should instead be administered TIV. An alternative inactivated vaccine, Fluzone High-Dose, contains 60 mcg of hemagglutinin antigen per influenza virus strain and is available for individuals aged 65 years and older. Individuals in this age group may receive either standard-dose TIV preparations or Fluzone High-Dose. Most TIV preparations are administered intramuscularly.
